top_categories.workout_context: 79 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Granfondo Ecuador's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Granfondo Ecuador's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before November.
Granfondo Ecuador's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 79 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Granfondo Ecuador. Train it until it feels boring.
At Granfondo Ecuador, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Base fitness for Granfondo Ecuador. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
The aerobic base that lets you ride mixed terrain at tempo for 79 miles without cracking. No shortcuts.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Granfondo Ecuador, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Granfondo Ecuador's mixed terrain actually does to you.

race_overlay.heat: November in Salinas, Santa Elena, Ecuador can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before Granfondo Ecuador. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for Granfondo Ecuador’s 79 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Granfondo Ecuador requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, TT Threshold, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 79 miles of mixed terrain in Salinas, Santa Elena, Ecuador.
